doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Playing brass bands: instruments, funerals and band arrangements
summary: Discussion of the eleven-piece brass band, E-flat horn, funerals, and how parts were split for trumpets and trombones.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You really liked the brass band?
I used to play a lot of fumes and parades. Did you ever play E-flat there and everything? Yeah, I got two E-flats home, I didn't have a condition. That's when I played E-flat. E-flat and everything?

I just used this and this and condition, you see. They had music and everything for it. And it was a music band. They didn't do much. They played a little by head but most of them music, marches and all that stuff, they had heavy funerals, you tell you. They had a real number one band for eleven pieces. We could have used a little more complemented entry. We just used one peckhorn, see, but we could have used another to bounce a little more. We used a baton, bass and a peckhorn, you see. And they'd have three trombones, I mean two trombones and two drums and three trumpets.
Some of the bands used two alto peckhorns then? Sometimes or not?

I don't remember none of them using two but they should have had two. It's good to have a crew. Yeah, it would have been nice if they could have used twelve, you know men? Yeah. And they had used two peckhorns to give that and a complement. It would be much better. When your grandmothers... Of course, I'll tell you another thing though, you know trombones, they give you a complement too on marches, few marches and things like that. So it's done pretty nice there. Because they used to write the parts that used to say first and second tenor, you see. And they'd give them two horns if they'd split the parts up. It'd come out nice because they used to write band music that way, huh?
You mean they'd play first and second parts?

Yeah, yeah. Well the trumpets used to have two solos and the first would be flat. Well naturally they would harmonize, you see, when one's up to, you know what I mean, two at the time. And the trombones, they used to have first and second tenors. Well the trombones could play that part, you see. I think it sounded pretty good when everybody was playing. For the eleven men, the bands used to do pretty good. And the Reading the Tuxedo band was pretty nice too. They used to play a lot of music.
